comments.note: No blocking issues — code is clean, well-structured, and maintainable. The extraction is a genuine improvement: config.js reducing from 1395 to 833 lines is a meaningful reduction in cognitive load. All functions are appropriately named (mr* prefix namespace is consistent), all guard clauses are present, and all user-visible strings are escapeHtml()-protected.

Fix-Forward applied: expanded the file header dependency comment on line 4 from 'Depends on: API, UI, escapeHtml, configDirty (defined in config.js)' to 'Depends on: API, UI, escapeHtml, crypto.randomUUID (browser built-in), configDirty (defined in config.js)'. crypto.randomUUID() is called directly at line 438 for new model ID generation and was absent from the listed dependencies. Non-behavioral — the runtime is unchanged. This change makes the dependency contract complete for future maintainers.

mrDeriveSlug() (lines 24-31) handles the chain of .replace() calls correctly and in the right order: lowercase → spaces-to-hyphens → strip non-alphanumeric/hyphens → collapse hyphens → trim leading/trailing hyphens. The slug regex (MR_SLUG_REGEX) and the derive function are consistent with each other. No edge-case gap identified.

mrHasChanges() (lines 47-56): the comparison iterates index-by-index rather than by ID. This is correct under the assumption that element order is preserved by mrDoSave() (which sends activeModels in iteration order) and the server reflects that order back in result.models. This assumption is implicitly upheld by the current API, but worth noting: if the server ever returns models in a different order (e.g. alphabetical), mrHasChanges() would always return true after a save, causing a spurious dirty indicator. Acceptable as-is for the current backend contract; documented here for the long view.

mrDoSave() (lines 503-564): the Save button is disabled at line 507 before the duplicate-slug check at line 511, but re-enabled at line 522 only in the duplicate-slug error path. The API .catch() at line 551 also re-enables the button. However, if the API call resolves with result.models present, the button is never explicitly re-enabled — it becomes irrelevant because mrRefreshTab() is called (line 546) which rebuilds the DOM and a freshly-wired button replaces it. This is correct but subtle; a future refactor that adds an optimistic-update path could break this. Current pattern is acceptable.

Add Model form empty-name guard (lines 431-434): when name is blank after slug validation passes, the handler only focuses the name input and returns — no error message is shown. This is slightly inconsistent with the inline-edit empty-name guard (which shows a '.mr-name-error' element). In practice the name placeholder text ('e.g. Claude Opus 4') makes the required field self-evident, so this is acceptable. A future pass could add a '.mr-add-name-error' element for full symmetry, but it is not blocking.

The load-order dependency (config-model-registry.js must precede config.js) is enforced only by the script ordering in index.html. There is no runtime guard that would surface a clear error if this order were reversed during a future index.html edit. For a vanilla-JS SPA this is standard practice and low risk; the header comment documents the constraint. If this SPA ever adopts a bundler, this implicit load-order contract must be the first thing converted to an explicit import.

[documentation-forward] mrHasChanges() performs an index-based comparison (not ID-based). This silent assumption — that the server returns models in the same order as submitted — should be captured in an inline comment on the function explaining why index-based comparison is correct and when it would break. A short note such as '/* Assumes server preserves element order. If order is ever server-sorted, compare by ID map instead. */' would be sufficient.
